chapters: Unit 2: Communication with Family and Friends
Unit 6: Why Do We Like Stories?
lessons:
Vocabulary: identity, personality, values, background, beliefs, character, confidence, strength, weakness, curious, self-respect, self-discovery, unique, popular, honest.
- background: where someone comes from • identity: who a person is • self-discovery: learning more about who you are • value: to have a high opinion of something.
Grammar: Present perfect (active): have / has + past participle.
Example: I have studied English since I was six.
Present perfect (passive): have / has + been + past participle.
Example: The museum has been visited by many tourists.
Use "since" with a point in time (since 2020) and "for" with a period of time (for three years).
Common words: just, already, yet, ever, never.
Story: "Who Am I Beyond My Looks" (Ahmed from Giza), "The Mirror Moment" (Nour and her portraits), and The School Garden Project, chapter one (Zeina).

Vocabulary: communicate, communication, connection, misunderstanding, bond, supportive, respectful, resolve, siblings, distant, awkward, frustrated, gesture, reconnect, meaningful, face-to-face.
- misunderstanding: failure to understand correctly • bond: a strong connection between people • siblings: brothers and sisters • awkward: uncomfortable or strange • gesture: a sign or action that shows feeling • frustrated: upset because of difficulty.
Grammar: The third conditional talks about unreal situations in the past.
Form: If + past perfect (had + past participle), would have + past participle.
Example: If we had communicated better, we wouldn't have argued.
Texts: "Stay Connected", "The Silent Dinner" (Omar's family), and chapter two of the garden story (Zeina's proposal to the student council).

Vocabulary: Artificial Intelligence (AI), robot, advanced, limits, tasks, emotions, behavior, humans, innovation, compose, creative, customize, instantly, confused, notice, initiative, donations, quit, climate.
- advanced: very modern or developed • limit: the point where something stops • customize: change something to make it the way you want • instantly: without any delay.
A robot is a machine that can move and do tasks; AI is the "brain" that lets it learn and make decisions.
Grammar: Future simple active: will + base verb (Father will fix his car tomorrow).
Future simple passive: will + be + past participle.
Example: The test will be corrected by the teacher.

Vocabulary: screen time, entertainment, expert, balance, physical, useful, smart, focused, modern, distraction, scrolling, reduce, waste.
- physical: related to the body • expert: a person who knows a lot about something • balance: to keep things in the right amount • distraction: something that takes attention away.
Grammar: Modal verbs: must (obligation), mustn't (prohibition), can / could (permission or ability), should (advice).
Examples: Students must come to school on time. You mustn't make noise in the library. You should take breaks from the screen.
Connectors: although, however, on the other hand, because, so.
Example: Although it was raining, we went outside.

Vocabulary: designer, problem, solution, prototype, test, feedback, brainstorm, define, challenge, creativity, stylish, schedule, practical, sprint, ideation, point of view.
- prototype: a simple model of a design • creativity: the ability to make new ideas • stylish: attractive in a fashionable way • practical: effective or suitable.
Design thinking steps: understand the users (empathize), define the problem, brainstorm ideas, build a prototype, then test and improve.
Grammar: Sequence adverbs: first, then, next, after that, finally.
Imperatives: positive (Brainstorm many ideas.) and negative (Don't judge ideas during brainstorming.).

Vocabulary: moral, various, empathy, aware, spark, critically, conflict, respond, ambition, courage, symbol, point of view.
- moral: related to what is right or wrong • critically: in a careful thoughtful way • spark: to start or cause something • empathy: the ability to understand and share feelings • ambition: a strong desire to achieve something big.
Story elements: setting (where and when), characters, conflict (the problem), climax, solution (how the problem ends).
Types: fiction (imaginary), non-fiction (true), folk stories (traditional).
Grammar: Reported speech: tenses move one step back and pronouns change.
Examples: Sara said, "I will visit my grandmother tomorrow." → Sara said (that) she would visit her grandmother the next day.
Use "told" with an object: Ali told Omar that stories could teach him a lot.

bank.q: I ...... English since I was six.
bank.e: "since" + a point in time is used with the present perfect: have studied.

bank.q: The museum ...... by many tourists.
bank.e: Present perfect passive: has + been + past participle.

bank.q: They have lived in Giza ...... ten years.
bank.e: Use "for" with a period of time (ten years).

bank.q: Has she started her new job ......?
bank.e: "yet" is used in questions and negatives, at the end of the sentence.

bank.q: The task has ...... out already.
bank.e: Passive: has been + past participle (carried).

bank.q: "Where someone comes from" means:
bank.e: background = where someone comes from; identity = who a person is.

bank.q: "Learning more about who you are" is called:
bank.e: self-discovery = learning more about yourself.

bank.q: A journalist needs to be ...... to look for new news.
bank.e: curious = wanting to know and learn things.

bank.q: Sama's ...... helps her overcome different situations.
bank.e: strength helps you overcome life's challenges.

bank.q: Being a talented programmer, Rodina soon became ...... in the world of technology.
bank.e: popular = liked or known by many people.

bank.q: In "The Mirror Moment", Nour found comfort in her:
bank.e: Nour was quiet at school and found comfort only in her sketchbook.

bank.q: The visitors have ...... left.
bank.e: "just" comes between have/has and the past participle: have just left.

bank.q: In The School Garden Project, Zeina felt sad because the playground was:
bank.e: It was large but empty and gray, with concrete ground and trash.

bank.q: "Something that makes you feel sad" means:
bank.e: depressing = making you feel sad.

bank.q: They ...... to Alexandria. It's their first visit.
bank.e: Present perfect with "never" for experiences: have never been.

bank.q: If she had left early, she ...... the train.
bank.e: Third conditional: would have + past participle (caught).

bank.q: If Ahmed ...... more, he would have passed the exam.
bank.e: The if-clause in the third conditional uses the past perfect.

bank.q: If we had brought the map, we ...... lost.
bank.e: Result clause: would (not) have + past participle.

bank.q: The third conditional talks about:
bank.e: It imagines a different past and its different result.

bank.q: "A strong connection between people" means:
bank.e: bond = a strong connection.

bank.q: I have three ......: two brothers and a sister.
bank.e: siblings = brothers and sisters.

bank.q: "Failure to understand correctly" is a:
bank.e: misunderstanding = failure to understand correctly.

bank.q: "Feeling uncomfortable or strange" means:
bank.e: The silence at Omar's dinner table made everything feel awkward.

bank.q: "Feeling upset because of difficulty" means:
bank.e: frustrated = upset due to difficulty.

bank.q: "A sign or action that shows feeling or intent" is a:
bank.e: gesture = a sign or action that shows a feeling.

bank.q: Showing care and regard for others means you are:
bank.e: respectful = showing care and regard.

bank.q: In "The Silent Dinner", Omar and his parents became distant because of:
a: school stress, phone distractions and arguments
bank.e: They were busy and distracted, so the dinner table became silent.

bank.q: Good communication includes words, tone of voice, facial expressions and:
bank.e: Communication isn't only about words; it includes body language too.

bank.q: "A plan or suggestion for others to consider" is a:
bank.e: Zeina wrote a simple proposal for the school garden.

bank.q: The test ...... by the teacher tomorrow.
bank.e: Future simple passive: will + be + past participle.

bank.q: Robots will ...... to do important tasks.
bank.e: After "will" use "be" + past participle in the passive.

bank.q: Father ...... his car tomorrow.
bank.e: Future simple active: will + base verb.

bank.q: The problem will be solved ...... the engineer.
bank.e: In the passive, the doer comes after "by".

bank.q: "Very modern, developed or complex; not basic" means:
bank.e: advanced = very modern or developed.

bank.q: "The point where something stops or cannot go further" is a:
bank.e: Understanding emotions is one of the limits of AI.

bank.q: "Without any delay" means:
bank.e: instantly = immediately, without delay.

bank.q: To change something to make it the way you want is to:
bank.e: The robot teacher said lessons will be customized for each student.

bank.q: AI can ...... music and write poetry.
bank.e: compose = create or produce (music, poems).

bank.q: According to the reading, the difference between a robot and AI is that:
a: a robot is a machine that moves and does tasks, and AI is the brain that helps it learn
AI can move but robots can't
bank.e: AI is the "brain" that can go inside a robot.

bank.q: "Taking action without waiting for others" means:
bank.e: Zeina showed initiative by asking the community for donations.

bank.q: "Money or gifts given to help a project" are:
bank.e: donations = money or gifts given to help.

bank.q: "Invention and improvement" is the meaning of:
bank.e: innovation = new ideas, inventions and improvements.

bank.q: Students ...... come to school on time.
bank.e: must = obligation.

bank.q: You ...... make noise in the library.
bank.e: mustn't = prohibition (it is not allowed).

bank.q: You ...... take breaks from the screen. It's good for your eyes.
bank.e: should = advice.

bank.q: ...... it was raining, we went outside.
bank.e: Although joins two contrasting ideas in one sentence.

bank.q: Technology helps us. ......, it causes some problems.
bank.e: "On the other hand" introduces the opposite point.

bank.q: "Related to the body" means:
bank.e: physical = related to the body.

bank.q: "A person who knows a lot about something" is an:
bank.e: expert = a specialist.

bank.q: "Something that takes attention away" is a:
bank.e: Screens can be a big distraction if you are not careful.

bank.q: "To keep things in the right amount" means:
bank.e: We should balance screen time with other activities.

bank.q: Staying ...... during class helps us learn more.
bank.e: focused = not easily distracted.

bank.q: Too much ...... time can affect sleep and mood.
bank.e: Spending too long on screens affects sleep, energy and mood.

bank.q: Fun activities like games or watching TV are called:
bank.e: entertainment = fun activities.

bank.q: Which is a useful kind of screen time?
bank.e: Not all screen time is the same; schoolwork and learning skills are useful.

bank.q: "A simple model of a design" is a:
bank.e: Designers build a prototype to test their ideas.

bank.q: "The ability to make new ideas" is:
bank.e: creativity = the ability to produce new ideas.

bank.q: "Attractive in a fashionable way" means:
bank.e: stylish = fashionable and attractive.

bank.q: "Effective or suitable" means:
bank.e: practical = effective and suitable for real use.

bank.q: "Brainstorming or coming up with ideas" is called:
bank.e: ideation = the process of creating ideas.

bank.q: The first step of design thinking is to:
a: understand the users and what they need
bank.e: First, see through the users' eyes; then define, brainstorm, prototype and test.

bank.q: ...... hesitate. Trust your abilities.
bank.e: Negative imperative: Don't + base verb.

bank.q: ...... your time and effort.
bank.e: Positive imperative starts with the base form of the verb.

bank.q: ...... judge ideas during brainstorming.
bank.e: During brainstorming, all ideas are welcome: Don't judge ideas.

bank.q: First, define the problem. ......, brainstorm many solutions.
bank.e: Sequence adverbs show order: first, then, next, finally.

bank.q: To ...... means to clearly state the problem you want to solve.
bank.e: define = state the problem clearly.

bank.q: In "See through Their Eyes", Omar spent a day with Karim to:
bank.e: His teacher said: First, see through their eyes.

bank.q: She is ...... to her studies and does her homework on time.
bank.e: dedicated = committed and hard-working.

bank.q: Sara said, "I will visit my grandmother tomorrow." → Sara said that she ...... her grandmother the next day.
bank.e: In reported speech "will" becomes "would" and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

bank.q: Hana said, "I am studying science now." → Hana said that she ...... science then.
bank.e: Present continuous moves back to past continuous; "now" becomes "then".

bank.q: Ayman ...... Rodayna that she could go shopping.
bank.e: Use "told" + object (told Rodayna); "said" has no direct object.

bank.q: Dr. Salwa said, "I lived in Sohag two years ago." → She said that she ...... in Sohag two years before.
bank.e: Past simple moves back to past perfect; "ago" becomes "before".

bank.q: "Related to what is right or wrong in behavior" means:
bank.e: Stories often teach a moral or life lesson.

bank.q: "In a careful and thoughtful way; not just accepting things" means:
bank.e: Stories help people think more critically.

bank.q: To start or cause something to happen is to:
bank.e: The story sparked his interest in history.

bank.q: The ability to understand and share someone's feelings is:
bank.e: Reading stories builds empathy.

bank.q: "A strong desire to achieve something big" means:
bank.e: Zeina's ambition became bigger than just a garden.

bank.q: The problem in a story is called the:
bank.e: Story elements: setting, characters, conflict, solution.

bank.q: "Where and when the story happens" is the:
bank.e: setting = the place and time of the story.

bank.q: Stories made up with imaginary characters are:
bank.e: Fiction is imaginary; non-fiction is based on real events.

bank.q: In "The Clever Fox", the fox wanted the crow's:
bank.e: The fox praised the crow to make her sing and drop the cheese.

bank.q: Once upon a time, there ...... a brave knight.
bank.e: Stories are usually told in the past simple.

bank.q: In the last chapter of the garden story, Zeina was chosen:
bank.e: She learned that real leadership means helping others and being honest.
